about: Plain-language HPD reference built ONLY from these official NYC sources (read 2026-11-21): HPD ABCs of Housing (2021 PDF), HPD Heat and Hot Water page, NYC311 KA-01036, HPD window guards press release (014-25), HPD Indoor Allergen Hazards page (Local Law 55), HPD asthma/leaks press release (030-25). owner_responsible: yes | no | depends | unclear. 'unclear' = the sources do not clearly cover it. rules.py rules take priority over this table.

rows.condition: Heat during the day (6 AM to 10 PM)
rows.plain_rule: From October 1 to May 31, between 6 AM and 10 PM, if it is below 55°F outside, the owner must keep your home at least 68°F.

rows.condition: Heat at night (10 PM to 6 AM)
rows.plain_rule: From October 1 to May 31, between 10 PM and 6 AM, the owner must keep your home at least 62°F, no matter how warm it is outside.

rows.condition: No heat in summer (June to September)
rows.plain_rule: Heat is only required from October 1 to May 31.
The owner must give you hot water 24 hours a day, every day of the year, at least 120°F.
The owner must provide heat, hot and cold water, good lighting, and security measures, and tenants should have electricity.
The owner must install smoke detectors in each apartment.
The owner must install at least one carbon monoxide detector in each apartment, within 15 feet of the door to each bedroom.
Tenants must keep smoke and CO detectors working, like changing batteries. If you removed one, you must put it back.
In buildings with 3 or more apartments, the owner must install window guards on all windows where a child 10 or younger lives, except windows to a fire escape.
If you ask in writing, the owner must install window guards even if no young children live with you.
Tenants must tell the owner (on the yearly form) if a child 10 or younger lives there, let them in to install guards, and never remove guards.

rows.condition: Locks or window gates that need a key from inside
rows.plain_rule: Door locks and window gates that need a key from inside to open are illegal and must be removed.
Your apartment's front door and the building's entrance and stair doors must close by themselves.
Owners must fix leaks quickly. Roofs, outside walls, and plumbing must be kept in good repair.

rows.condition: Leaking pipes, blocked or broken drains
rows.plain_rule: Leaking water pipes and stopped-up or broken drains are urgent repairs the owner must make.
In buildings with 3 or more apartments, the owner must keep your home free of mold and fix what causes it, like leaks.
Tenants should keep the home clean and dry, use fans or open windows in bathrooms and kitchens, and tell the owner about leaks and mold.
In buildings with 3 or more apartments, the owner must keep your home free of mice, rats, and cockroaches and seal the holes they come through.
Owners must use a licensed pest control company to treat bedbugs. HPD can issue a violation if an inspector sees live bedbugs.
Tenants should keep food in sealed containers, cover garbage, take it out daily, and cut down clutter.

rows.condition: Peeling paint with a child under 6
rows.plain_rule: In buildings built before 1960 with 3 or more apartments, if a child under 6 lives there, the owner must find and safely fix lead paint hazards like peeling paint.
Tell your landlord about peeling paint. If they don't fix it, or fix it in an unsafe, dusty way, call 311.
If a child under 6 lives there, the owner must give you knob covers for a gas stove (unless you refuse in writing).
A gas leak is an emergency: leave the building and call 911. Leaking gas pipes or appliances are urgent repairs.

rows.condition: Appliances not working (stove burner, refrigerator, dishwasher, washer/dryer)
rows.plain_rule: The official guides we use do not say whether the owner must repair appliances like a stove, fridge, dishwasher, or washer.
The official guides we use say tenants should have electricity, but do not cover broken outlets or wiring in detail.

rows.condition: Windows or doors that are stuck or broken (other than guards, gates, self-closing doors)
rows.plain_rule: The official guides we use say homes must be safe and well kept, but do not say exactly which window or door repairs are required.

rows.condition: Damage caused by the tenant or guests
rows.plain_rule: Tenants may not damage the building, on purpose or by neglect, and are responsible for what their guests do.

rows.condition: Letting the owner in for repairs
rows.plain_rule: Tenants must let the owner in to inspect and repair. The owner must tell you in writing first (weekdays 9 AM to 5 PM), except in emergencies like leaks.
